blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: Prehistory represents the vast span of human existence prior to the development of written records.
The classification of the Prehistoric Age is primarily determined by the evolution of tools, materials, and living patterns.
Analyzing the basis of prehistoric classification helps trace early technological progress and human adaptation.

blocks.content: Prehistory refers to the long span of human past before the invention of writing. Since writing had not yet developed, historians cannot rely on inscriptions, manuscripts, or literary sources to understand this period. Instead, the reconstruction of prehistoric life depends entirely on archaeological evidence such as stone tools, bones, fossils, cave paintings, and habitation sites.
In competitive examinations like , a very clear distinction is made: - History deals with written records. - Prehistory deals with periods where no written records exist.
This distinction is extremely important for objective-type questions.
Basis of Classification of the Prehistoric Age

The Prehistoric Age is classified mainly on the basis of the tools used by humans. As humans progressed, their tools became more refined, which also reflects changes in their lifestyle and social organisation.

items: Competitive exams frequently ask for the specific criteria used to differentiate prehistoric sub-periods.
Be prepared to distinguish between Prehistory, Protohistory, and History based on written source availability.
